tasks.//typecheck:features: The PUBLISHED feature sets `deno task typecheck` cannot see. `cargo check --workspace` resolves features unified and with defaults ON, so `tsv_ts`'s `convert` is always enabled there — while `@fuzdev/tsv_format_wasm` builds `--no-default-features --features format`, where `tsv_ts::ast::convert` does not exist. An unconditional reference to a convert-gated item therefore compiles clean through the whole gate and fails in CI at `build:packages`, which is the only place those feature sets are built (and it builds them for wasm32, a target `check` deliberately never touches). Both combinations are checked NATIVELY here because the failure is feature resolution, not codegen — no wasm32 toolchain needed, ~1 s warm.
tasks.typecheck:features: cargo check -p tsv_wasm --no-default-features --features format && cargo check -p tsv_wasm --no-default-features --features parse
tasks.//typecheck:js: Typechecks the JS/TS the repo owns — the bench harness, scripts/, and the tsv_debug Deno sidecar — which `deno task typecheck` (cargo) does not see. Directory arguments, not per-directory globs: deno walks them (skipping node_modules) so a new subdirectory is covered the day it appears, where a glob list silently is not. The sidecar is a second invocation because it takes neither the harness config nor its node_modules — and it needs `--no-lock`, since it imports npm by specifier and would otherwise MINT a root deno.lock in a repo that is deliberately lock-free (benches/js/deno.json already sets `lock: false` for the first leg). NOT in `deno task check`: the harness imports npm packages by bare specifier, so this needs `deno task bench:install`, and CI's check job deliberately installs no node_modules (.github/workflows/check.yml). The node-modules-free scripts/ half is carved out into typecheck:scripts, which DOES gate — so what only this task covers is benches/js, the sidecar, and scripts/doctor.ts. Same posture as test:deno:canonical — run it after a harness, scripts, or sidecar change.
tasks.typecheck:js: deno check --config benches/js/deno.json benches/js scripts && deno check --no-lock crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/sidecar.ts
tasks.//typecheck:scripts: The scripts/ half of typecheck:js, carved out so it CAN gate in `check`: nothing else typechecks the release scripts, and `deno run` does not — so publish.ts / publish_napi.ts / build_napi_packages.ts, whose first real execution is a release, would otherwise reach it unchecked. Node-modules-free by construction, which is what lets it run on CI's clean checkout: every scripts/ module resolves to relative paths and node: builtins. The ONE exception is `scripts/doctor.ts`, whose corpus probe reaches benches/js/lib/corpus.ts and its bare `@fuzdev/fuz_util` import — it is excluded below so this stays a DIRECTORY walk (a new script is covered the day it appears, where a file list silently is not), and typecheck:js still covers it under the bench config. `--no-lock`: the repo is deliberately deno.lock-free.

tasks.//bench:runtimes: Preflight for the aggregates: the three-runtime tasks NEED node and bun, and without this they discover a missing one ~8 minutes in — after regenerating two of the three siblings and skipping `bench:compose`, which leaves the committed combined report stale against fresh siblings and reading as a two-runtime run. Deno is the only hard dependency of the repo; a machine without node or bun runs the per-runtime tasks instead, which is what the message says. Each check is PARENTHESIZED: `a || b && c || d` binds left-associatively, so the flat form runs the second `||` arm after the first one failed and reports BOTH runtimes missing when only one is. ⚠ The node arm asks what the binary IS, never whether the NAME resolves: `deno task` prepends its node-compat shim directory (`~/.cache/deno/node_compat_bin`, holding a `node` symlink to the deno binary) to PATH, so `which node` succeeds inside every deno task on a machine with no node at all. That shim also RUNS the harness — `current_runtime()` then reports `deno`, and `bench:node` overwrites `report.deno.*` instead of producing a node sibling, which is the exact silent two-runtime run this preflight exists to stop. `globalThis.Deno` is the tell the shim cannot hide. The same probe asserts the VERSION the message names, so the ≥22.18 requirement is checked rather than merely stated — below it `node benches/js/bench.ts` fails on the first type annotation it reads, naming the syntax instead of the runtime.
tasks.bench:runtimes: (node -e 'if (globalThis.Deno) process.exit(1); const [a, b] = process.versions.node.split(".").map(Number); if (a < 22 || (a === 22 && b < 18)) process.exit(1)' 2> /dev/null || (echo '✗ bench needs node (>=22.18, native TS type-stripping) — a real node, not the deno node-compat shim — install it, or run the per-runtime tasks: deno task bench:deno' && exit 1)) && (which bun > /dev/null || (echo '✗ bench needs bun — install it, or run the per-runtime tasks: deno task bench:deno && deno task bench:node && deno task bench:compose' && exit 1))
tasks.//bench:perf: Builds the whole artifact set ONCE, then measures it under each runtime with the `:run` legs (freshness-guarded, so the order is provable rather than assumed). Chains `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` and NOT the suite harvests: the corpus VIEWS decide who needs which cache, and the perf view holds only the `real`-tier svelte_styles cache (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests).
tasks.bench:perf: deno task bench:runtimes && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run && deno task bench:node:run && deno task bench:bun:run && deno task bench:compose
tasks.//bench:deno: Every standalone per-runtime leg (`bench:deno` / `bench:node` / `bench:bun`, and `bench:conformance`) builds the WHOLE artifact set, not its own half. Each leg REPORTS the same tsv binary-size rows, cross-binding by design: `binary_sizes.ts` sizes the tsv artifacts by PATH rather than by the impl registry, so the deno report carries `tsv (napi)` and the node/bun reports the `tsv (ffi)` trio. Built per half, a leg would size the other half at whatever commit it was last built while sizing its own at HEAD, inside sibling reports all stamped with one `git_commit`. `lib/check_artifact_freshness.ts` warns when a `:run` leg is about to do exactly that (`warn_stale_reported_artifacts`); building everything is what makes the warning unreachable here. Warm, the other half costs about a second (`run_if_stale` skips each wasm-pack, cargo no-ops).
tasks.bench:deno: deno task build:bench && deno task bench:deno:run
tasks.//rsvelte-allow-run: The rsvelte-fmt row spawns a prebuilt binary (it ships no in-process API — see benches/js/lib/rsvelte.ts), so `bench:deno:run` and `smoke` must permit it by path. All five published platform packages are listed because the task string is static while the installed one is per-machine; Deno ignores a nonexistent path entry silently (unlike a bare NAME, which logs a resolution failure), so the four that don't apply cost nothing. Node and Bun need no equivalent.

tasks.//bench:harvest: Two groups, split because their consumers differ (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests is the full argument). `bench:pins:suites` is the conformance-view group: the four SUITE caches (wpt / test262 / ts-repo / svelte-rejects) plus the CSS reject PIN, which harvests nothing but is stamped and graded the same way — all `--if-present`, so each warn-skips a checkout it cannot see, which is what lets the group preflight `conformance` on a partial machine. `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` is the perf-view group of one: unstamped (live dev repos, ~2 s), a MINIMUM pin with a drift band, and it FAILS rather than warn-skips on a missing dev repo. This task stays the manual refresh-everything entry point.

tasks.//wire:audit: The WIRE-INJECTION audit: the parse-side sibling of gaps/blanks. Those inject into a fixture and grade the FORMATTER; this injects into every Svelte input and grades the resulting WIRE against the canonical parser (benches/js/lib/wire_inject.ts). It exists because every other injection audit is self-referential — idempotency, reparse, no-panic — while the one real external oracle, corpus:compare:parse, only ever saw inputs someone had already written. A hand-rolled scan can therefore be wrong about a spelling no fixture and no real repo contains, which is exactly where two block-annotation bugs lived. Each injected variant is graded against its OWN base file, so a fixture that diverges on purpose contributes nothing. TWO families, and they differ in COVERAGE because they differ in site density: `wire:audit` widens whitespace inside tag/block heads (where tsv hand-rolls its scanning) and runs as a CENSUS (`--inject-limit 0`, every one of ~11k sites, ~17 s) — the sampled form it used to run hid 8x its findings (3 files vs 25) and redrew its sample on every fixture edit; `wire:audit:terminators` injects a lone CR / U+2028 / U+2029 anywhere, the spellings on which the two `loc` line classes DISAGREE — the one axis no fixture can carry (the format path folds a raw CR) and no real repo contains, and whose model is mirror-knowledge held by hand at seven call sites in tsv's Svelte parser. ⚠️ CURRENTLY RED BY DESIGN, like compile:fuzz — a discovery tool with an open work list (a `//` comment's extent is clipped at a trimmed slice boundary in the bounded-slice tag readers), not a regression gate, so it is not in `check`. Needs the canonical parser, so it is conformance-tier. ⚠️ The terminator family is a 5.9% SAMPLE of its ~629k sites and therefore cannot be ratcheted: the stride divisor is each file's own site count, so one unrelated one-line fixture edit was measured retiring 12 of its 194 finding signatures with every underlying bug intact. A census there costs ~9 minutes; the ws family's costs seconds, which is the whole difference.

tasks.//conformance: The sidecar-cadence aggregate. `fixtures:validate` and `compile:fixtures:validate` preflight it as the ORACLE-FRESHNESS legs: `deno task check` runs each fixture tree's sidecar-free slice via cargo test, which grades tsv against the COMMITTED `output_prettier.*` / `expected_server.js` and so stays green when tsv and the committed file drift away from the live oracle together. Only a run that re-formats through prettier itself can see that — 17 s for all 4227 parser/formatter fixtures, which is why it gates here rather than living in a command someone has to remember. It cannot gate in `check`: that job runs on a bare CI checkout with no npm install, and the sidecar resolves its oracles from npm. `bench:pins:suites` preflights ahead of them as the PIN-FRESHNESS leg: the conformance-view count pins it re-derives are graded by no other cadence (docs/gate_counts.md §Where the numbers live), and it is ordered after `pins:audit:checkouts` (which names the checkout that moved) and before the fixture legs, so a corpus move is reported before anything expensive runs — seconds when nothing moved, and each leg warn-skips an absent checkout so a partial machine still reaches the legs below. `bench:harvest:svelte-styles` runs later, beside the corpus legs that read its cache: it loads the PERF view, where every dev repo is REQUIRED, so it fails rather than warn-skips — the same requirement `corpus:compare` imposes a step later (benches/js/CLAUDE.md §Harvests).
tasks.conformance: deno task pins:audit:checkouts && deno task bench:pins:suites && deno task fixtures:validate && deno task compile:fixtures:validate && deno task bench:harvest:svelte-styles && deno task build:ffi:corpus && TSV_FFI_PROFILE=corpus PRETTIER_DEBUG=1 deno run --allow-ffi --allow-read --allow-env --allow-net --allow-sys --allow-run=cargo --allow-write=benches/js/.cache benches/js/conformance.ts
